rounds.text: Central Mine Planning & Design Institute Ltd exhibits world-class capital efficiency, underpinned by an exceptional ROCE of 38.1% [E12] and a 3-year median ROE of 33% [E21], which drastically outpaces the sector median ROCE of 13.6% [E68]. Growth fundamentals remain robust over medium horizons, supported by a 3-year compounded sales growth rate of 19% [E15] and a 3-year compounded profit growth rate of 27% [E18], alongside an operating margin expansion to 34% in Mar 2026 [E23]. Financial health is pristine with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x [E31] and an impressive cash conversion of 1.17x for Mar 2026 where operating cash flows reached Rs 716 Cr and free cash flow hit Rs 652 Cr [E27, E28, E29]. Furthermore, intrinsic valuation metrics such as the discounted cash flow model point to fundamental undervaluation at an intrinsic value of Rs 261 against a market price of Rs 239 [E38], while historical relative strength registers a perfect score of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E44]. Conceded: institutional money flow indicates negative momentum with a holding change of -3.98 percentage points [E37] and quarterly operating margins compressed to 30% in Jun 2026 from 45% a year prior [E24].

The valuation rests on thin ice given that the stock trades at an expensive price-to-book multiple of 7.47x against a book value of ₹ 32.0 [E2], and at 7.65x compared to a sector benchmark of just 2.42x [E7]. Profit momentum has turned sharply negative, highlighted by a -8% contraction in compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E19], a severe -58% YoY net profit drop flagged by the screen engine [E60], and a plummeting quarterly operating margin of 30% in June 2026 compared to 45% in the year-ago quarter [E24]. Institutional investors are actively deserting the stock, resulting in negative money flow [E37] driven by foreign institutions cutting stakes from 1.21% to 0.50% [E35] and domestic institutions slashing holdings from 11.12% to 7.85% [E36]. Furthermore, the company suffers from glaring operational friction with high debtors of 169 days [E54], an inconsistent yearly and quarterly margin trend [E25, E26], and a price sitting below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E43]. Conceded: the company maintains a robust return on equity track record with a 3-year median of 33% [E21], robust operating cash flows of Rs 716 Cr backed by strong cash conversion [E27, E28], and a conservative near-zero debt-to-equity structure [E31].

Conceded: the price-to-book multiple is elevated at 7.47x against a sector benchmark of 2.42x [E2, E7]. However, this premium valuation is fully justified by superior capital efficiency, as demonstrated by an outstanding ROCE of 34.83% and a 5-year median ROE of 32% [E10, E20]. Conceded: trailing twelve-month profit growth shows a -8% contraction [E19]. That short-term blip is overshadowed by a multi-year sales uptrend with 3-year compounded sales growth at 19% and 3-year compounded profit growth at 27% [E15, E18, E56]. Conceded: institutional holdings have contracted through outflows [E35, E36, E37]. Such temporary institutional rotation ignores the pristine balance sheet featuring a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x and robust free cash flow of Rs 652 Cr [E29, E31]. Finally, while the June 2026 quarterly margin compressed to 30% [E24], the company operates as a non-cyclical business where seasonal weakness in June is expected, and working capital requirements have structurally improved from 135 days to 99.2 days [E49, E52].

Conceded: the 3-year compounded sales growth is 19% and 3-year compounded profit growth is 27% [E15, E18]. However, that multi-year uptrend has abruptly reversed in the trailing twelve months, where compounded profit growth has plunged to -8% and screeners flag sharp year-over-year quarterly declines of -58% in net profit and -35% in sales [E19, E60, E61]. Conceded: the balance sheet carries a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x and generates Rs 652 Cr in free cash flow [E29, E31]. Yet, this financial strength is completely overshadowed by severe operational inefficiencies, notably high debtors of 169 days alongside an inconsistent yearly and quarterly operating-margin trend [E25, E26, E54]. Conceded: the 5-year median ROE sits at 32% and ROCE at 34.83% [E10, E20]. Despite these high returns, the stock trades at an exorbitant price-to-book ratio of 7.47x against a sector benchmark of 2.42x, while institutional money flow reads negative with foreign and domestic institutions aggressively reducing their stakes by a combined 3.98 percentage points [E2, E7, E35, E36, E37]. Finally, dismissing the June 2026 margin compression to 30% as seasonal ignores the reality that operating margins suffered a massive 15 percentage-point year-over-year drop, and the stock currently trades below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E24, E43].
